description: A graduate study of how clouds are built and run: hypervisors, cluster schedulers, isolation, elasticity, storage and the economics of operating at scale. Students design and break architectures in the cloud console, measure them with queueing and cost models, and defend their trade-offs in a design review.
modelledOn: Barroso, Clidaras and Holzle, The Datacenter as a Computer
Burns, Beda and Hightower, Kubernetes: Up and Running and the Kubernetes design documents
Well-Architected Framework guidance from the major public cloud providers
outcomes: Explain how hypervisors and containers virtualise CPU, memory and I/O, and compare their performance and isolation.
Analyse cluster scheduling policies for fairness, utilisation and packing efficiency.
Design a multi-tenant architecture with defined isolation boundaries and a documented threat model.
Build and evaluate autoscaling policies using queueing models and control theory against realistic workloads.
Produce a costed multi-region cloud architecture with SLOs, failure modes and a justified set of trade-offs.

units.title: Hypervisors and resource virtualisation
topics: CPU virtualisation: trap-and-emulate, binary translation and hardware-assisted virtualisation
Memory virtualisation: shadow page tables, nested paging, ballooning and page sharing
I/O virtualisation: emulated devices, virtio and SR-IOV passthrough
Containers versus VMs: namespaces, cgroups, microVMs and unikernels
Live migration: pre-copy, post-copy and downtime analysis
VM placement as bin packing and the economics of overcommit

units.title: Cluster scheduling and orchestration
topics: Orchestrator architecture: API server, state store, scheduler, kubelet and controllers
Scheduling algorithms: filter and score, bin packing, affinity, taints and tolerations
Fairness and priority: dominant resource fairness, queues, preemption
Monolithic, two-level and shared-state schedulers; scaling to thousands of nodes
Declarative reconciliation loops, operators and custom resources
Cluster networking: overlays, service discovery and service meshes

units.title: Multi-tenancy and isolation
topics: Tenant threat models: noisy neighbours, side channels and escape attacks
Isolation mechanisms: hypervisor, user-space kernels, microVMs, seccomp and capabilities
Network isolation: virtual private clouds, security groups and microsegmentation
Resource isolation: quotas, cgroup limits, QoS classes and rate limiting
Tenancy models for SaaS: silo, pool and bridge; tenant-aware identity and metering

units.title: Autoscaling and elasticity control
topics: Workload modelling: arrival processes, burstiness and diurnal patterns
Queueing models for capacity: M/M/1, M/M/c and Little's law
Reactive autoscaling: threshold rules, target tracking and cooldown
Control-theoretic autoscaling: PID, delay, oscillation and stability
Predictive autoscaling with time-series forecasts
Serverless scaling: cold starts, concurrency limits and scale to zero

units.title: Cloud storage architecture
topics: Object, block and file storage: interfaces, performance and use cases
Replication versus erasure coding; durability and availability arithmetic
Consistency models: eventual, causal and strong; quorum reads and writes
Distributed block storage and data placement across failure domains
Caching tiers and content delivery networks
Backup and disaster recovery: RPO, RTO and recovery drills

units.title: Cost and performance engineering
topics: Pricing models: on-demand, reserved, spot; committed use and break-even analysis
The FinOps cycle: tagging, showback, chargeback and unit economics
Performance models: Amdahl's law, the universal scalability law and tail latency
Right-sizing and benchmarking instance families
Data gravity: egress charges, region choice and placement
Service level objectives, error budgets and capacity planning

units.title: Edge and multi-cloud design
topics: Edge and fog computing: latency budgets and cloudlets
Hybrid and multi-cloud: portability, lock-in and abstraction costs
Global traffic management: DNS steering, anycast and geo-replication
Data sovereignty and Africa-region design under constrained connectivity
Failure domains, blast radius and chaos engineering

units.title: Architecture review and design project
topics: Reviewing against the pillars: reliability, security, cost, performance and operations
Designing a national e-service platform for Ghana
Failure injection and trade-off analysis of the design
Presenting and defending an architecture decision

schedule.title: CPU, memory and I/O virtualisation
schedule.exercise: Explain why x86 originally could not be trapped-and-emulated, how nested paging removes the cost of shadow page tables, and when SR-IOV beats virtio.

tasks.title: Check the virtualisation extensions and hypervisor flags on a Linux VM, then list which guest instructions need trapping
Overcommit memory on three VMs sharing one host in the console, trigger ballooning, and record the guest slowdown
Compare disk and network throughput of emulated, virtio and passthrough devices on the same instance, and explain the differences

schedule.title: Containers, migration and placement
schedule.exercise: Compute downtime for pre-copy live migration of an 8 GB VM with a given dirty rate, and pack 40 VMs onto the fewest hosts with and without 1.5x CPU overcommit.

tasks.title: Create a process in its own namespace with a memory limit through cgroups and show it is confined
Live-migrate a running VM between hosts under write load and measure total migration time and downtime
Code first-fit-decreasing and best-fit VM placement for 200 VMs, compare hosts used, and add an overcommit ratio to see the risk

schedule.title: Orchestrator architecture and scheduling
schedule.exercise: Trace what happens from submitting a pod to it running, and apply dominant resource fairness to three tenants with different CPU and memory demands.

tasks.title: Deploy a three-replica workload on a small cluster and list which component created, scheduled and started each pod
Use node affinity and taints to force a database pod onto a labelled node and show an unschedulable pod's reason
Implement dominant resource fairness for three users with CPU and memory demands and compare the allocation with plain CPU fair-share

schedule.title: Scheduler designs, reconciliation and networking
schedule.exercise: Compare monolithic, two-level and shared-state schedulers on scheduling latency and conflict rate, and write a controller loop in pseudocode that keeps five replicas running.

tasks.title: Delete a pod owned by a deployment and watch the controller recreate it, noting the events in order
Trace a packet from a pod to a service across two nodes in an overlay network and record each encapsulation step
Simulate a shared-state scheduler with optimistic concurrency, measure the conflict rate as load grows, and compare with a single scheduler

schedule.title: Multi-tenancy and isolation
schedule.exercise: Write a threat model for a SaaS platform hosting rival schools' records on shared infrastructure, and choose silo, pool or bridge tenancy for each layer with reasons.

tasks.title: Set CPU and memory quotas on two tenants sharing a host and show one tenant's load no longer slows the other
Place two tenants in separate virtual networks with security groups and prove with connection tests that they cannot reach each other
Respond to a case where a tenant sees another's data, trace the isolation failure from the evidence, and choose containment and redesign steps

schedule.title: Workload models and reactive autoscaling
schedule.exercise: Fit a Poisson arrival rate to hourly request counts for a mobile money API, use M/M/c to find servers for a 200 ms mean response, and compare with a threshold rule.

tasks.title: Configure an autoscaling group on 60 percent CPU target and drive load up and down to see instances added and removed
Compute mean response time with M/M/c for 1 to 10 servers at a given arrival rate and plot the knee as utilisation nears one
Generate a bursty diurnal request trace, replay it against threshold autoscaling, and report SLO violations and instance-hours

schedule.title: Control-theoretic, predictive and serverless scaling
schedule.exercise: Explain why a scaling loop with a five-minute start-up delay oscillates, and design a predictive policy that pre-warms capacity before a daily salary-day peak.

tasks.title: Invoke a serverless function after idle periods and record cold-start versus warm latency for ten calls
Simulate a PID-controlled instance count with a start-up delay, and find gains that avoid oscillation after a load step
Forecast the next hour of load with a seasonal model, drive a predictive scaler, and compare its cost and violations with reactive scaling

schedule.title: Storage types, durability and consistency
schedule.exercise: Compute annual durability for 3-way replication versus a 10+4 erasure code given a disk failure rate and repair time, and decide which consistency model a ledger needs.

tasks.title: Store the same data in an object bucket, a block volume and a file share, and compare latency and access method for each
Compute the probability of data loss for replication and erasure coding as disk failure rates and repair times vary
Step through quorum reads and writes with N=5 across partitions and find settings of R and W that give strong or only eventual consistency

schedule.title: Data placement, caching and disaster recovery
schedule.exercise: Place replicas across racks and zones so that losing any one zone loses no data, size a CDN cache for a 5 percent hot set, and write an RPO and RTO plan for a hospital system.

tasks.title: Put a content delivery cache in front of a bucket and compare latency and origin load for the first and later requests
Implement hash-based data placement across zones and check that losing any single zone leaves every object readable
Fail a primary region during a drill, restore from replicated backups, and measure achieved RPO and RTO against a stated target

schedule.title: Pricing, FinOps and performance models
schedule.exercise: Compute the break-even utilisation for reserved against on-demand instances, tag a bill by team and product, and apply the universal scalability law to measured throughput.

tasks.title: Price a fixed workload on on-demand, reserved and spot instances in the calculator and tabulate the monthly cost of each
Tag resources by team in a sample account, produce a showback report, and find three untagged cost items to assign
Fit the universal scalability law to throughput measured at 1 to 32 nodes and predict the node count where adding more reduces throughput

schedule.title: Right-sizing, data gravity and SLOs
schedule.exercise: Right-size a fleet from utilisation traces, estimate the monthly egress bill of serving video from the wrong region, and compute the error budget for a 99.9 percent SLO.

tasks.title: Compute allowed downtime per month for 99, 99.9 and 99.99 percent availability and the error budget left after two incidents
Benchmark a workload on three instance families, compute cost per request for each, and pick the cheapest that meets latency
Compare serving a dataset from a nearby region against a cheaper distant one, including egress and replication charges, and justify the choice

schedule.title: Edge, multi-cloud and resilience
schedule.exercise: Design traffic steering for a service with users in Accra, Lagos and Nairobi, state which data must stay in-country, and list the failure domains whose loss you can survive.

tasks.title: Configure a load balancer across two zones, take one down, and confirm users are served by the other
Compare round-trip latency from a clinic to a distant region and to an edge site over a lossy link, and decide which runs the inference
Inject zone, database and dependency failures in sequence into a three-tier design, record the blast radius of each, and fix the worst weakness

schedule.title: Architecture review and design project
schedule.exercise: Present a national e-service architecture to a review panel with its cost model, SLOs, failure analysis and the three trade-offs you made, then answer questions.

tasks.title: Draw an architecture diagram for a given web service and mark where each pillar of the review checklist is addressed or missing
Build the core of a national service across two zones with autoscaling, storage and identity roles, then estimate its monthly bill
Defend your design to a review panel scenario, answering challenges on cost, resilience and data residency, and revise a decision in response
